rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh was seized and made an example of: God drowned him in this world and will punish him in the next.
rows.anchor: بأن أغرقه في الدنيا ويعذبه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reads the punishment as retribution for Pharaoh’s final claim, “I am your highest lord,” and earlier claim that he knew no god but himself.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه فعاقبه الله بكلمته الآخرة وكلمته الأولى

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A report from Abu Jaʿfar says forty years separated Pharaoh’s two statements.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير عن أبي جعفر ع أنه كان بين الكلمتين أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Pharaoh invoked his claim to divinity while asking his people to protect him from a snake; fearing harm and seeking help disproves divinity.
rows.anchor: فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى فامنعوني من هذا الثعبان ولم يعلم الجهال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Moses asking why Pharaoh was spared for four hundred years despite blasphemy; God answers that Pharaoh was courteous and hospitable, so God repaid him for that.
rows.anchor: عن وهب عن ابن عباس قال قال موسى ع

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report through Abu Jaʿfar quotes the Prophet recounting Gabriel’s question about Pharaoh; God says only one afraid of missing out makes such a claim.
rows.anchor: روى أبو بصير عن أبي جعفر ع قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال جبرائيل ع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s fate is a lesson and evidence for anyone who fears God and His punishment, enabling the discerning to distinguish truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى ويخاف عقابه ونقمته ودلالة يمكن أن يعتبر بها العاقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Moses follows mention of those who denied prophets and resurrection, consoling Muhammad, urging patience after Moses, warning his people, and reinforcing the proof.
rows.anchor: وجه اتصال قصة موسى ع بما قبلها أنه لما تقدم ذكر المكذبين للأنبياء المنكرين للبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s claim to be the only one who can harm others and cannot be harmed is false; this is an attribute of God, creator of Pharaoh and all creatures.
rows.anchor: وكذب واللعين إنما هذه صفة الله الذي خلقه وخلق جميع الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Pharaoh made idols his lords and claimed to be both their lord and his people’s.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه جعل الأصنام أربابا فقال أنا ربها وربكم

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿAsim, except al-Aʿsha and al-Barjumi, reads فتَنفعَه in the accusative; the others read it nominative.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم غير الأعشى والبرجمي فتنفعه بالنصب والباقون بالرفع

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز
rows.claim: The Hijaz readers geminate the ṣad in تصدى; the others pronounce it lightly.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الحجاز تصدى بالتشديد والباقون تصدى بتخفيف الصاد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A noncanonical reading attributed to al-Hasan has أن جاءه as an interrogative.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة الحسن أن جاءه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir reads تصدى with a prefixed ḍamma and تلهى likewise with a prefixed ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقراءة أبي جعفر الباقر ع تصدى بضم التاء وفتح الصاد وتلهى بضم التاء أيضا

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة وشعيب بن أبي حمزة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa and Shuʿayb ibn Abi Hamza read نشره without the alif.
rows.anchor: وقراءة أبي حيوة وشعيب بن أبي حمزة نشره بغير ألف

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli explains the nominative as coordination with an earlier nominative; the accusative makes the clause a response with faʾ because the preceding statement is non-positive.
rows.anchor: من قرأ فتنفعه بالرفع عطفه على ما تقدم من المرفوع

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The accusative reading is illustrated by Moses’ statement, “so that I may reach the means … and look.”
rows.anchor: وكذا قوله لعلي أبلغ الأسباب أسباب السماوات فأطلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تصدى means to turn toward or expose oneself to someone; doubling assimilates the deleted initial ta, while the light reading drops one ta from تتصدى.
rows.anchor: أي تعرض فمن قرأ بتشديد الصاد أدغم التاء في الصاد

rows.speaker: ابن فليح والبزي عن ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Fulayh and al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir geminate the ta in تلهى, treating a separated form like a connected one and allowing a still consonant after a glide.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن فليح والبزي عن ابن كثير تلهى بتشديد التاء على أنه شبه المنفصل بالمتصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the interrogative reading, the sense is “Has the blind man just come to him?”; an omitted clause is supplied from عبس وتولى.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ أن جاءه بلفظ الاستفهام فتقديره الآن جاءه الأعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the common reading, فإن جاءه is governed by the nearest verb تولى: he turned away because the blind man came.
rows.anchor: وأما على القراءة المشهورة فإن جاءه في موضع نصب بتولى لأنه الفعل الأقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading of تصدى is understood as worldly adornment and tidings drawing one to attend to the wealthy; تلهى correspondingly means turning away from the blind man.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ تصدى فالمعنى يدعوك داع من زينة الدنيا وبشارتها إلى التصدي له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صحف is the plural of صحيفة; Arabs call anything written on a صحيفة or a book, whether on parchment or another material.
rows.anchor: الصحف جمع صحيفة والعرب تسمي كل مكتوب فيه صحيفة كما تسميه كتابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: السفرة are scribes of wisdom books; the singular سافر and the term سفر derive from uncovering, as in a woman uncovering her face, and can mean reconciling people.
rows.anchor: السفرة الكتبة لأسفار الحكمة واحدهم سافر وواحد الأسفار سفر وأصله الكشف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poet uses السفارة for mediation among one’s people, supporting the sense of reconciliation.
rows.anchor: وما أدع السفارة بين قومي وما أمشي بغش إن مشيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Prophet is described as possessing tremendous character and not harshness, the apparent subject of عبس وتولى may be someone else.
rows.anchor: وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم [القلم: 4]

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq reports that the passage was revealed about an Umayyad man with the Prophet who scowled and turned away when Ibn Umm Maktum arrived.
rows.anchor: روي عن الصادق ع أنها نزلت في رجل من بني أمية كان عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the passage concerns the Prophet, scowling at a blind man is not sinful because he cannot see it; God may still admonish the Prophet toward the highest manners and prioritize guiding a believer over courting a polytheist.
rows.anchor: فالجواب أن العبوس والانبساط مع الأعمى سواء إذ لا يشق عليه

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says an act may become sinful through a later prohibition, but its earlier occurrence was not thereby sinful; the prohibition came only now.
rows.anchor: وقال الجبائي: في هذا دلالة على أن الفعل يكون معصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Ibn Umm Maktum behaved discourteously and deserved to be ignored, but God rebuked the response because he might think poverty caused the rejection and status won the leaders’ welcome.
rows.anchor: إن ما فعله الأعمى نوعا من سوء الأدب فحسن تأديبه بالإعراض عنه

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq reports that the Prophet welcomed Ibn Umm Maktum warmly, saying God would never rebuke him on his account, and treated him with such kindness that he restrained himself for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع أنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عبس means to frown or contract the face, and تولى means to turn one’s face away.
rows.anchor: عبس } أي بسر وقبض وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind man might become purified through good works and learning, or remember and heed Qurʾanic admonition so that the reminder benefits his religion.
rows.anchor: أي لعل هذا الأعمى { يزكى } يتطهر بالعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God shows great courtesy: He does not directly say “you frowned,” but shifts to direct address only after passing over the frown.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا لطف من الله عظيم لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ لم يخاطبه في باب العبوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who considers himself self-sufficient is a prominent, wealthy person among his people.
rows.anchor: أي من كان عظيما في قومه واستغنى بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تصدى means to approach or attend to the wealthy person.
rows.anchor: أي تتعرض له وتقبل عليه بوجهك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet bears no responsibility if the wealthy man does not accept Islam and leave disbelief; his duty is only to convey.
rows.anchor: فإنه ليس عليك إلا البلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man who comes eagerly, strives for good, and fears God is Ibn Umm Maktum.
rows.anchor: أي يعمل في الخير يعني ابن أم مكتوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تلهى means to disregard the blind man and occupy oneself with someone else.
rows.anchor: أي تتغافل وتشتغل عنه بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا commands the Prophet not to repeat this conduct; the Qurʾanic verses are a reminder, and whoever wishes may take heed of the revelation or admonition.
rows.anchor: أي إن آيات القرآن تذكير وموعظة للخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that whoever wishes may remember indicates that a person can act and choose freely.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أن العبد قادر على الفعل مخير فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition establishes that the conduct is impermissible in the future; the earlier act preceded the prohibition and was not a sin.
rows.anchor: وأما الماضي فلم يتقدم النهي عن ذلك فيه فلا يكون معصية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the honored pages as books with God, namely the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: في كتب معظمة عند الله وهي اللوح المحفوظ عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the honored pages with the books revealed to the prophets.
rows.anchor: يعني كتب الأنبياء المنزلة عليهم كقوله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Yaʿqub read تعرف in the passive with نضرة nominative; the others read it actively with نضرة accusative.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ويعقوب تعرف بضم التاء وفتح الراء نضرة بالرفع

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi alone reads خاتمه; this is also attributed to ʿAli and ʿAlqama, while the others read ختامه.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وحده خاتمه وهي قراءة علي ع وعلقمة والباقون ختامه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وحفص
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Hafs read فكهين without an alif; the others read فاكهين.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وحفص فكهين بغير ألف والباقون فاكهين

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi assimilate the lām into the thāʾ in هثوب الكفار; a similar reading is reported from Abu ʿAmr, while others pronounce it distinctly.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي هثوب الكفار بإدغام اللام في الثاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active and passive readings of تعرف في وجوههم convey the same meaning.
rows.anchor: تعرف في وجوههم على الخطاب والمعنى في القراءتين سواء

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda glosses ختامه as its conclusion, citing Ibn Muqbil’s verse about a sealed wine vessel.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: ختامه أي عاقبته

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli explains ختامه مسك as the drink’s fragrant, delicious finish, joining its aroma and pleasant taste.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: ختامه مسك والمراد به لذاذة المقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description is compared with drinks mixed with camphor or ginger, which sharpen the tongue’s taste.
rows.anchor: وكان مزاجها زنجبيلا [الإنسان: 17]

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi takes خاتمه to mean its end, as خاتم النبيين means the last of the prophets; ختام is a verbal noun and خاتم an active participle.
rows.anchor: وأما قول الكسائي خاتمه فإن معناه آخره كما كان خاتم النبيين معناه آخرهم

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says Abu ʿAmr’s assimilation in هثوب الكفار is acceptable because the sounds are close, though less so than lām into rāʾ; assimilation into shīn is also attested in poetry.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه: أدغم أبو عمرو هثوب الكفار وإدغامها فيها حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIlliyyun conveys height upon height; its emphatic wāw-nūn plural glorifies it and likens its high, majestic ranks to rational beings.
rows.anchor: عليون علو على علو مضاعف ولهذا جمع الواو والنون تفخيما لشأنه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says ʿIlliyyun names the highest places and has plural-like inflection because it is shaped like a plural, as in Qansarin.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: عليون اسم لأعلى الأمكنة وإعرابه كإعراب الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem uses a plural form to signify successive, uncounted showers, illustrating the form’s grandeur.
rows.anchor: فأصبحت المذاهب قد أذاعت به الإعصار بعد الوابلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأرائك are beds set within canopies.
rows.anchor: والأرائك الأسرة في الحجال والرحيق الشراب الذي لا غش فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الرحيق is a drink without impurity or adulteration.
rows.anchor: والرحيق الشراب الذي لا غش فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exhortation to work for this reward is linked to the parallel wording in al-Saffat.
rows.anchor: لمثل هذا فليعمل العاملون

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets the exhortation as a call for contenders to vie for it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فليتنازع المتنازعون عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam understands it as a call for those who desire something to compete eagerly for it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فليتشاح المتشاحون عن زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith promises that one who fasts for God on a hot day will be given sealed nectar to drink when thirsty.
rows.anchor: من صام لله في يوم صائف سقاه الله على الظمأ من الرحيق المختوم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In his testament to ʿAli, the Prophet says that one who leaves wine for God will be given sealed nectar.
rows.anchor: ومن ترك الخمر لله سقاه الله من الرحيق المختوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasnim is a spring in Paradise and its most excellent drink; the described drink is mixed with it.
rows.anchor: أي ومزاج ذلك الشراب الذي وصفناه وهو ما يمزج به من تسنيم

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masruq says those brought near drink Tasnim unmixed, while it is mixed into the cups of the people of the right to make them pleasant.
rows.anchor: قال مسروق يشربها المقربون صرفا ويمزج بها كأس أصحاب اليمين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When asked about Tasnim, Ibn Abbas connects it to what God has hidden as comfort for the eyes in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وروى ميمون بن مهران أن ابن عباس سئل عن تسنيم فقال هذا مما يقول الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan calls Tasnim one of the hidden things God has kept for the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قول الحسن خفايا أخفاها الله لأهل الجنة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Tasnim is a drink that pours down onto the people of Paradise from above.
rows.anchor: هو شراب ينصب عليهم من علو انصبابا عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Tasnim is a river flowing in the air and pouring into the vessels of Paradise’s inhabitants as needed.
rows.anchor: هو نهر يجري في الهواء فينصب في أواني أهل الجنة بحسب الحاجة عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Ibn Abbas say the spring is pure for those brought near, while the rest of Paradise’s people drink it mixed.
rows.anchor: أي هي خالصة للمقربين يشربونها صرفا ويمزج لسائر أهل الجنة عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are Quraysh disbelievers and elites such as Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil; the believers are the Prophet’s companions, including ʿAmmar, Khabbab, and Bilal.
rows.anchor: يعني كفار قريش ومترفيهم كأبي جهل والوليد بن المغيرة والعاص بن وائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers laughed at the believers mockingly and derisively in this world.
rows.anchor: على وجه السخرية بهم والاستهزاء في دار الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that they mocked the believers’ earnest worship, frequent prayer, and fasting because they denied judgment and resurrection.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ضحكوا من جدهم في عبادتهم وكثرة صلاتهم وصيامهم لإنكارهم الجزاء والبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that they expressed disbelief and astonishment at the claim of resurrection and the revival of decayed bones.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون كان ضحكهم إنكارا وتعجبا من قولهم بالإعادة وإحياء العظام الرميمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that extreme disbelief and ignorance led them to mislead ordinary people into thinking the Muslims were wrong.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ذلك لغلوهم في كفرهم وجهلهم ولإيهام العوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the believers passed them, the disbelievers signaled to one another with their eyes and eyebrows in mockery.
rows.anchor: بأن يشير بعضهم إلى بعض بالأعين والحواجب استهزاء بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a counterpart to the believers’ reward, God or the angels may ask whether the disbelievers have received their due, reminding believers of the painful punishment earned by disbelief and mockery and increasing their joy; believers may also say it to one another.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه جاء في مقابلة ما فعل بالمؤمنين أي هل ثوب الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These proposed speakers and purposes fit only the interpretation that the question begins a new, independent sentence rather than continuing the preceding one.
rows.anchor: وكل هذه الوجوه إنما تتجه على القول الأول إذا كانت الجملة كلاما مستأنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shafaq is the delicate red glow in the west after sunset; the root conveys tenderness, and related usage describes compassion, fear for something, or thin cloth.
rows.anchor: فالشفق هو الحمرة الرقيقة في المغرب بعد مغيب الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited lines describe the red color of twilight and a cup whose contents resemble twilight, illustrating the color sense.
rows.anchor: على الزمان بكأس حشوها شفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasq means gathering; the gathered food is abundant and measurable by volume or weight, with a stated measure of sixty sāʿ, and ittisaq is complete gathering.
rows.anchor: والوسق الطعام المجتمع الكثير مما يكال أو يوزن ومقداره ستون صاعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭabaq means a state or circumstance; Arabs call calamities أم طبق or بنات طبق.
rows.anchor: وأصل الطبق الحال والعرب تسمي الدواهي أم طبق وبنات طبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem calls successive hardships one طبقا after another, illustrating ṭabaq as a changing condition.
rows.anchor: إني امرؤ قد حلبت الدهر أشطره وساقني طبق منه إلى طبق

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the response to إذا is indicated by فملاقيه; the pronoun can refer to the Lord or to a person’s labor and deed.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: جواب إذا يدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative grammatical view takes إلى as meaning لام.
rows.anchor: قيل: إن هنا إلى بمعنى اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers construing إلى according to the phrase’s meaning: the person is striving toward God.
rows.anchor: والوجه الصحيح فيه أن يكون محمولا على المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible construction attaches إلى to an omitted phrase: a person labors for himself and arrives at his Lord.
rows.anchor: على أنه يحتمل أن يكون إلى متعلقة بمحذوف ويكون التقدير أنك كادح لنفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is compared with تبتل إليه, understood as turning from creation back to God or desiring Him.
rows.anchor: يكون على معنى تبتل من الخلق راجعا إلى الله تعالى أو راغبا إليه

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Qatada and Mujahid connect the earth’s casting out its burdens with the parallel statement that the earth brings forth its loads.
rows.anchor: وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها [الزلزلة: 2] عن قتادة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth empties itself, leaving nothing in its interior; alternatively, it casts out its buried treasures and minerals and clears its surface of mountains and seas.
rows.anchor: أي خلت فلم يبق في بطنها شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated obedience formula concerns heaven first and earth second; these are major portents of the Hour, after which a person will see the good or evil sent ahead, as 84:6 indicates.
rows.anchor: ليس هذا بتكرار لأن الأول في صفة السماء والثاني في صفة الأرض وهذا كله من أشراط الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to every accountable descendant of Adam: each person labors through hardship in deeds and carries that work to God.
rows.anchor: خطاب لجميع المكلفين من ولد آدم يقول الله لهم سبحانه ولكل واحد منهم يا أيها الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meeting the recompense is described as meeting the deed itself, magnifying its importance.
rows.anchor: أي ملاق جزاءه جعل لقاء جزاء العمل لقاء له تفخيما لشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the pronoun to mean meeting the Lord and coming under His judgment, since He alone judges.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ملاق ربك أي صائر إلى حكمه حيث لا حكم إلا حكمه

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري والبلخي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari and al-Balkhi make أذنت لربها وحقت the response to إذا, with an extra wāw; the author rejects this as weak in favor of فملاقيه.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري والبلخي: جواب إذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person given the record in the right hand receives an easy account: he is not pressed over good deeds and their reward or burdens removed through repentance or pardon.
rows.anchor: يريد أنه لا يناقش في الحساب ولا يواقف على ما عمل من الحسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view defines easy accounting as overlooking sins and rewarding good deeds; a prophetic report says whoever is closely examined is punished, and another says the person’s deeds are shown before pardon.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الحساب اليسير التجاوز عن السيئات والإثابة على الحسنات ومن نوقش الحساب عذب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says three traits bring an easy account and admission to Paradise through God’s mercy: give to one who deprived you, maintain ties with one who cut you off, and forgive one who wronged you.
rows.anchor: ثلاث من كن فيه حاسبه الله حسابا يسيرا وأدخله الجنة برحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view describes successive hardships: life, death, resurrection, and recompense; this interpretation is reported as a Prophetic narration.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه شدة بعد شدة حياة ثم موت ثم بعث ثم جزاء وروي ذلك مرفوعا

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAta reads it as one condition following another, with alternating ease and hardship, poverty and wealth, and health and illness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمرا بعد أمر ورخاء بعد شدة وشدة بعد رخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view traces the stages of human life from a drop of semen through old age and death, listing thirty-seven names for the person’s stages.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حالا بعد حال نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة ثم عظما ثم خلقا آخر

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Makḥul interprets the phrase to mean that something unlike a person’s present state will happen every twenty years.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لتحدثن أمرا لم تكونوا عليه في كل عشرين سنة عن مكحول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes it as ascent from level to level: good leads to greater good and corruption to greater corruption, since each thing draws toward its like.
rows.anchor: منزلة عن منزلة طبقة عن طبقة وذلك أن من كان على صلاح

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda, also reporting it from al-Sadiq, says people will follow the ways of earlier communities and undergo what they underwent, exactly alike.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لتركبن سنن من كان قبلكم من الأولين وأحوالهم عن أبي عبيدة وروي ذلك عن الصادق ع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes Quraysh disbelievers: without faith in Muhammad and the Qurʾan, they have no bliss or honor.
rows.anchor: بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن والمعنى أي شيء لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it expresses astonishment at their failure to believe despite clear evidence and asks what excuse or impediment they could have.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه فما وجه الارتياب الذي يصرفهم عن الإيمان وهو تعجب منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question continues: what prevents them from believing and prostrating to God when the Qurʾan is recited?
rows.anchor: أي ما الذي يصرفهم عن الإيمان وعن السجود لله تعالى

rows.speaker: عطاء والكلبي
rows.claim: ʿAta and al-Kalbi interpret their not prostrating as not praying to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى لا يسجدون لا يصلون لله تعالى عن عطاء والكلبي

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet recited إذا السماء انشقت and prostrated.
rows.anchor: وفي خبر مرفوع عن أبي هريرة قال قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reject the Messenger and Qurʾan by following their ancestors and leaders, not because the evidence is unclear or insufficient.
rows.anchor: أي لم يتركوا الإيمان لقصور في البيان أو لانقطاع من البرهان لكنهم قلدوا أسلافهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Muqatil say God knows the disbelief and idolatry they gather and conceal in their hearts.
rows.anchor: أي يجمعون في صدورهم ويضمرون في قلوبهم من التكذيب والشرك عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the phrase covers the good and bad deeds they gather.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بما يجمعون من الأعمال الصالحة والسيئة عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ derives الإيعاء from placing something in a container; hearts hold what they acquire of knowledge or ignorance.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: أصل الإيعاء جعل الشيء في وعاء

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A saying of ʿAli calls hearts containers and says the best are those with the greatest capacity.
rows.anchor: وفي كلام أمير المؤمنين ع إن هذه القلوب أوعية فخيرها أوعاها

words: إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ
rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿAmir, ʿAsim, and Hamza read لما with a geminated mīm; the others read it lightly.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة لما عليها بتشديد الميم والباقون بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A noncanonical reading attributed to Ibn Abbas has مهلهم رويدا without an alif.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة ابن عباس مهلهم رويدا بغير ألف

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: For the light reading, Abu ʿAli takes أن as a lightened emphatic particle, its lām as the lām of emphasis, and ما as extra, like examples in other verses; it still receives an oath.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: من خفف لما كانت أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī also reports Abu ʿAli’s analysis that the geminated form treats إن as negative and لما as إلا, with the clause accepting an oath, parallel to another Qurʾanic usage.
rows.anchor: ومن ثقل " لما " كانت أن عنده النافية كالتي

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan says the heavy form of إن means إلا, though Arabs scarcely recognize this usage.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: الثقيلة في معنى إلا والعرب لا تكاد تعرف ذا

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says he does not know the basis for the geminated reading.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: لا أعرف وجه التثقيل

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAwf says that when he read the geminated إن كل نفس لما before Ibn Sirin, Ibn Sirin rejected it.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عوف قال قرأت عند ابن سيرين إن كل نفس لما بالتشديد فأنكره

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says لما can mean إلا in two settings: here and in the oath expression سألتك لما فعلت, meaning ألا فعلت.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: استعملت لما في موضع إلا في موضعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaraq means to come at night and originally to knock; a mallet strikes, a road is beaten by passersby, and the night visitor knocks to announce arrival.
rows.anchor: طرقني فلان إذا أتاني ليلا وأصل الطرق الدق ومنه المطرقة لأنها يدق بها

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet forbade a man to arrive unexpectedly at night before an absent wife can prepare herself and a disheveled woman can comb her hair.
rows.anchor: ونهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يطرق الرجل أهله ليلا حتى تستحد المغيبة

rows.speaker: هند بنت عتبة
rows.claim: Hind bint ʿUtba’s poem calls her group daughters of Ṭariq, meaning their father is a star in honor and elevation.
rows.anchor: وقالت هند بنت عتبة: نحن بنات طارق نمشي على النمارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem warns that calamities may come in the pre-dawn hours, illustrating the verb for an event arriving at night.
rows.anchor: يا راقد الليل مسرورا بأوله إن الحوادث قد يطرقن أسحارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najm means a star appearing in the sky; anything that emerges may be called nājim, by analogy with sprouting plants, teeth, and horns.
rows.anchor: والنجم الكواكب الطالعة في السماء يقال لكل طالع ناجم تشبيها به نجم النبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaqib means shining and luminous, evoking a flame lit by its light; it can also mean lofty and very high.
rows.anchor: والثاقب المضيء النير وثقوبه توقده بنوره والثاقب العالي الشديد العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dafq is a forceful, abundant pouring; the reproductive fluid is called dāfiq for flowing and pouring out.
rows.anchor: والدفق صب الماء الكثير باعتماد قوي ومثله الدفع فالماء الذي يكون منه الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical explanation takes ماء دافق to mean مدفوق, like a concealed secret or a pleasing life.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ماء دافق معناه مدفوق ومثله سر كاتم وعيشة راضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarāʾib are the areas of the chest and the singular is tarība; the term is associated with their softened movement, like soil.
rows.anchor: والترائب نواحي الصدر واحدتها تريبة وهو مأخوذ من تذليل حركتها كالتراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath is by the heaven itself, or alternatively by the Lord of heaven; al-Ṭabrisī says the issue was discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: والسماء } أي بالسماء. وقيل: برب السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭariq is whatever comes at night; the Prophet would not know which referent was intended until God clarified it as the piercing star.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن هذا الاسم يقع على كل ما طرق ليلا ولم يكن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يدري

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the piercing star generally with the collective of stars.
rows.anchor: ويريد به العموم وهو جماع النجوم عن الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies it as Saturn, lofty above the other stars.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو زحل والثاقب العالي على النجوم عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views identify the piercing star as the Pleiades, which Arabs call the star, or the moon because it rises at night.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد به الثريا والعرب تسميه النجم

words: إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s answer means every soul has a guardian angel who records its words, acts, and all good and evil it acquires; on the light reading, each is indeed guarded.
rows.anchor: أي ما كل نفس إلا عليها حافظ من الملائكة يحفظ عملها وقولها وفعلها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the guardian angel preserves a person’s deeds, provision, and lifespan.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: حافظ من الملائكة يحفظ عملها ورزقها وأجلها

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The address targets one who denies resurrection: reflect on the source and manner of human creation to recognize that the One who began it from a drop can restore it.
rows.anchor: يعني المكذب بالبعث عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The human is created from semen, poured into the woman’s womb and from which the child develops.
rows.anchor: أي من ماء مهراق في رحم المرأة يعني المني الذي يكون منه الولد عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says Hijaz usage often gives an active participle a passive sense, as in a concealed secret, they are made ready, and a sleeping night.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: وأهل الحجاز يجعلون الفاعل بمعنى المفعول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas locates the emergence between the backbone and the chest area where a necklace rests.
rows.anchor: وهو موضع القلادة من الصدر عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAta says the reference is the man’s backbone and the woman’s ribs, since a child comes from both fluids.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال عطاء يريد صلب الرجل وترائب المرأة والولد لا يكون إلا من الماءين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the tarāʾib are the hands, feet, and eyes.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الترائب اليدان والرجلان والعينان عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: When asked about tarāʾib, ʿIkrima points to the chest between the breasts.
rows.anchor: وسئل عكرمة عن الترائب فقال هذه ووضع يده على صدره بين ثدييه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid locates the tarāʾib between the shoulders and chest; the common Arabic usage means the bones of the chest and neck.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما بين المنكبين والصدر عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والجبائي
rows.claim: The author prefers the explanation that God can resurrect a person after death, since the following verse speaks of the day hidden things are tested.
rows.anchor: يعني أن الذي خلقه ابتداء من هذا الماء يقدر على أن يرجعه حيا بعد الموت عن الحسن وقتادة والجبائي

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
rows.claim: An alternative says God can return the fluid to the backbone.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه تعالى على رد الماء في الصلب لقادر عن عكرمة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Another view says God can return the person to fluid as before.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه على رد الإنسان ماء كما كان قادر عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan interprets the return as God’s ability to reverse the person’s life stages from old age through youth and childhood back to semen.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: يقول إن شئت رددته من الكبر إلى الشباب ومن الشباب إلى الصبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse supports resurrection as the intended return: God can raise a person on the day inner secrets are exposed.
rows.anchor: أي أنه قادر على بعثه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secrets are human deeds and obligations kept between God and servant; on Judgment Day they are examined so fulfillment and neglect, good and evil, become clear.
rows.anchor: والسرائر أعمال بني آدم والفرائض التي أوجبت عليه وهي سرائر بين الله والعبد
